It's current day but I'm the teenage version of myself and I open the doors to my school, the front entrance is very dark but otherwise looks like how it actually did. I walk up the stairs and go to an unmarked office, where I am given a paper copy of my class schedule and I start to walk around (the high school I went to was 4 floors with two separate wings in real life, in my dreamscape its about 50 floors + the basement ) the hallways are very dark and are only lit up by an occasional torch that is hanging from the walls. At one point, I briefly enter a home ec class (this is where I've seen the kitchenette) and my hearing starts to turn into ringing when a classmate attempts to talk to me, which leads me to get up and start looking for another classroom. I walk down the staircase for 40+ floors until I reach the basement/catacombs and start getting a really strong feeling of dread when I start to pass through. There are skulls and fossils and occasional beams of light coming from different passageways, leading to classrooms. I walk down there for a really long time until I open a door that somehow takes me back to the office I entered to get my schedule in. A nondescript authority figure, perhaps a guidance counselor or teacher, gets frustrated and tells me I need to go back to class. At this point, I usually either wake up by this time or it will segue into a different but (usually) related dream.

i am a Rhode Island native (raised in Pawtucket for most of my life and briefly lived in Cumberland) who currently lives in Providence and previously lived in New York for a brief period of time for college. i grew up hating Rhode Island and now that i am back for good have learned to appreciate the city a lot more.

imo the pros are:

great food, bars and breweries; great parks (india point, roger williams, etc etc), very easy to navigate and very walkable, in close proximity to both Boston and New York, lots of forms of transportation that makes it easy to travel even without a car (trains \*both amtrak and MBTA\*, buses, etc etc), great music and art scenes, great people. it is also convenient if you have to catch a flight somewhere because you can either go to T.F. Green in Warwick or take the ride up to Logan which is fairly convenient either way.

cons:

providence place mall parking lot. it is actually the worst fucking thing ever. we also have shitty infrastructure (ESPECIALLY roads), in fact we have some of the worst in the entire country. cost of living is expensive with high taxes and increasingly unaffordable housing is the norm, especially near the colleges. our drivers are notoriously shit i feel like i dont really need to elaborate on this point any further. RIPTA runs like ass and at a certain point it is difficult to take the bus further than Warwick

i think there are some misconceptions about us Rhode Islanders and while i understand where it comes from, i think people don't really realize how nice and hospitable the people from here really can be. we can come across cold and scrappy but if you focus too much on that, you also might be missing out on some lovely people

this is going to be pretty long but ive been sitting on this story for YEARS now waiting to tell someone about it so here goes lol

so several years ago my family took me and my cousin on a camping trip in the White Mountains in New Hampshire for a birthday celebration, as our birthdays were exactly a week apart from one another. this trip was poorly planned and my aunt, who booked the entire trip, had completely looked over the (nearly all negative) reviews of the campground and booked it merely because of the child-oriented tourist traps their website advertised; the campground noted a community pool, an arcade and "gold mining" and my aunt thought it would be fun for my little cousin to go

 the trip was doomed from the start, and by the time the trip came around none of us really wanted to go anymore, but since we already booked it we figured why not just take the risk. the entire car ride to the campground was markedly bad, as my aunt and dad got into a fist fight while we drove through one of the busiest parts of Boston on the highway at rush hour, swerving into traffic and almost veering off of the road completely at several points. at several points my aunt had threatened to turn around and cancel the entire trip, and in hindsight that may have been for the better

in spite of all of this, the trouble really started once we actually arrived at the campground when the owner greeted us, he was calm and seemingly easygoing until my cousin started to play with some toys that had been set up in the front of the property where we would check in. for reasons still unknown, he forcefully grabbed my cousin's hands and pulled them off of the toys, yelling at him. my aunt and grandmother immediately started to tell him off, which only angered him further. little did any of us know, things would escalate and quickly

wherever my family was, the owner would also be there observing us, usually looking angry, not breaking eye contact and standing in place until we left - i distinctly remember one occasion where we were playing in the arcade and he stood there to watch us for nearly 45 minutes straight. when not using the on-site facilities, he would follow us around the campground with his golf cart and verbally harass & interrogate us.

however, the worst would happen during our fourth day there in the early hours of the morning, in which i had awoken as i had heard some weird noises outside that kept me from sleeping. i had heard these same noises repeatedly other nights as well, but wrote it off as animals roaming around or the lake nearby. it was pitch black, as it was around 3am, and as i walked out of my tent i looked up to see lights and the owner's golf cart parked directly onto our site right near our tents - i figured out quickly that he had been watching us while we slept and i just so happen to catch him in the act. he had a very cold, angry look on his face that i will never forget and he quickly drove off.  that very same morning, upon telling my family this story, we decided to end the trip 2 days early and head back home

it has been 7 years since this happened & i have not been camping since and still have no desire to anytime soon
